nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ and let $S$ be a permutation Wordle strategy (a permutation $S[m]$ of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ for each $m$) whose component $S[n]$ has no fixed point. For a secret permutation $\pi$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ let $\gamma_2$ be the second guess of $S$. The sum, over all derangements $\pi$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, of the number of positions $i$ with $\gamma_2(i) = \pi(i)$, divided by the number of derangements…
nodes.title: Average number of correct positions in the second guess

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 3$, exactly $2^n - (2n + 1)$ derangements $\pi$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ are guessed by the cyclic shift strategy in exactly three guesses.
nodes.title: Derangements solved in three guesses by cyclic shift

nodes.summary: Among inductive strategies, cyclic shift left minimizes three-guess solves first correct at guess two. Let $n \ge 4$ and let $S$ be an inductive strategy of length $n$ whose component $S[n]$ is not the left cyclic shift $i \mapsto i - 1 \pmod n$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Let $\mathrm{CSL}_n$ be the cyclic shift left strategy, whose component on $n$ positions is the left cyclic shift and whose component on $m \ne n$…
nodes.title: Among inductive strategies, cyclic shift left minimizes three-guess solves first correct at guess two

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 4$ and let $S$ be a permutation Wordle strategy (a permutation $S[m]$ of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ for each $m$) with $S[m]$ equal to the cyclic shift $j \mapsto j + 1 \bmod m$ for every $m < n$. The number of permutations $\pi$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that $S$ guesses in exactly three guesses and whose first guess (the identity) has a correct position, that is, $\pi$ has a fixed point, is…
nodes.title: Three-guess solves of permutations with a fixed point

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 4$ and let $S$ be a permutation Wordle strategy (a permutation $S[m]$ of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ for each $m$) whose component $S[n]$ is an $n$-cycle. Exactly one permutation $\pi$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is guessed by $S$ in exactly three guesses with the third guess being the first guess that has a correct position.
nodes.title: A unique three-guess solve with no early correct position

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 4$ and let $S$ be an inductive strategy of length $n$ whose component $S[n]$ is not the cyclic shift $j \mapsto j + 1 \bmod n$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then fewer than $2^n - 2n - 2$ permutations $\pi$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ are guessed by $S$ in exactly three guesses with the second guess being the first guess that has a correct position.
nodes.title: Upper bound on three-guess solves first correct at guess two

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 4$ and let $\mathrm{CSL}_n$ be the strategy whose component on $n$ positions is the left cyclic shift $j \mapsto j - 1 \bmod n$ and whose component on $m \ne n$ positions is the cyclic shift $j \mapsto j + 1 \bmod m$. The number of permutations $\pi$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that $\mathrm{CSL}_n$ guesses in exactly three guesses, with the second guess being the first guess that has a correct position, is…
nodes.title: Lucas-number count for the left-shift strategy

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 4$, the number of permutations $\pi$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that the cyclic shift strategy guesses in exactly three guesses, with the second guess being the first guess that has a correct position, is $2^n - 2n - 2$.
nodes.title: Three-guess solves of cyclic shift first correct at guess two

nodes.summary: For all $n$ and $m$ with $m \ne n$, the component on $m$ positions of the left-shift strategy $\mathrm{CSL}_n$ is the cyclic shift $j \mapsto j + 1 \bmod m$ of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$.
nodes.title: Non-top components of the left-shift strategy

nodes.summary: For every $n$, the component on $n$ positions of the left-shift strategy $\mathrm{CSL}_n$ is the left cyclic shift $j \mapsto j - 1 \bmod n$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the inverse of the cyclic shift $j \mapsto j + 1 \bmod n$.
nodes.title: Top component of the left-shift strategy

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the strategy $\mathrm{CSL}_n$ assigns to each $m$ a permutation of $m$ positions: for $m = n$ the left cyclic shift $[m, 1, 2, \dots, m-1]$ in one-line notation, that is, $i \mapsto i - 1 \pmod m$, and for every $m \ne n$ the right cyclic shift $[2, 3, \dots, m, 1]$, that is, $i \mapsto i + 1 \pmod m$.
nodes.title: Cyclic shift left strategy

nodes.summary: For every $m$, the component of the cyclic shift strategy on $m$ positions is the rotation $i \mapsto i + 1 \pmod m$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$.
nodes.title: Components of the cyclic shift strategy

nodes.summary: A strategy assigns to each $m$ a permutation of $m$ positions, used to rearrange the entries on the $m$ incorrect positions of a guess. The cyclic shift strategy $\mathrm{CS}$ has component $\mathrm{CS}[m] = [2, 3, \dots, m, 1]$ in one-line notation, that is, the rotation $i \mapsto i + 1 \pmod m$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$.
nodes.title: Cyclic shift strategy

nodes.summary: A strategy $S$ (a permutation $S[m]$ of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ for each $m$) is inductive of length $n$ when $S[m]$ is the rotation $i \mapsto i + 1 \pmod m$ for every $m < n$, and $S[n]$ is an $n$-cycle, that is, a single cycle moving every element of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.
nodes.title: Inductive strategy

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $S$ be a strategy whose component $S[m]$ has no fixed point for every $2 \le m \le n$, and write $[x^r] f_S$ for the number of permutations of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that $S$ guesses in exactly $r$ guesses. Then $[x^1] f_S = 1$ and $[x^2] f_S = 2^n - n - 1$, the Eulerian number $A(n, 1)$.
nodes.title: One- and two-guess counts for deranged strategies

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 4$ and let $S$ be an inductive strategy of length $n$ whose component $S[n]$ is not the left cyclic shift $i \mapsto i - 1 \pmod n$. Then strictly fewer permutations of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ are guessed in exactly three guesses with the cyclic shift left strategy $\mathrm{CSL}_n$ than with $S$.
nodes.title: Cyclic shift left minimizes three-guess solves among inductive strategies

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 4$ and let $S$ be an inductive strategy of length $n$ whose component $S[n]$ is not the rotation $i \mapsto i + 1 \pmod n$. Then strictly fewer permutations of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ are guessed in exactly three guesses with $S$ than with the cyclic shift strategy.
nodes.title: Cyclic shift maximizes three-guess solves among inductive strategies

nodes.summary: For every strategy $S$ and every $n$, write $f_S$ for the generating function whose coefficient $[x^r] f_S$ is the number of permutations of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that $S$ guesses in exactly $r$ guesses. Then the constant coefficient $[x^0] f_S$ vanishes.
nodes.title: No permutation is guessed in zero guesses

nodes.summary: For a strategy $S$ and natural numbers $n$ and $r$, the coefficient $[x^r] f_S(x)$ of the generating function of $S$ at length $n$ is the number of secret permutations of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that $S$ guesses in exactly $r$ guesses.
nodes.title: Coefficients of the guess-count generating function

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, a strategy $S$ and a permutation $\pi$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, write $\rho_S(\pi) = r$ when the $r$-th guess is the first guess with a correct position for the secret $\pi$. Then $\rho_S(\pi) = 1$, that is, the first guess (the identity) already has a correct position, exactly when $\pi$ has a fixed point.
nodes.title: Permutations with a correct entry in the first guess

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a strategy, that is, a permutation $S_m$ of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ for every $m$, let $\pi$ be a permutation of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $\gamma_1, \gamma_2, \dots$ be the guesses of permutation Wordle with strategy $S$ and secret $\pi$. For a natural number $r$, $\rho_S(\pi) = r$ means that $r \ge 1$, that $\gamma_r(k) = \pi(k)$ for some position $k$, and that for every $j$ with $1 \le j < r$ there is…
nodes.title: First guess with a correct position in permutation Wordle

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a strategy for permutation Wordle, that is, a permutation $S_m$ of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ for every $m$, and let $\pi$ be a permutation of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with no fixed point. Then the second guess $\gamma_2$ of permutation Wordle with strategy $S$ and secret $\pi$ is the inverse permutation $S_n^{-1}$.
nodes.title: The second guess against a derangement

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a strategy, that is, a permutation $S_m$ of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ for every $m$, let $\pi$ be a permutation of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $\gamma_1, \gamma_2, \dots$ be the guesses of permutation Wordle with strategy $S$ and secret $\pi$. For every $r \ge 1$, the guess $\gamma_{r+1}$ is the guess that one round of the game with strategy $S$ and secret $\pi$ produces from $\gamma_r$.
nodes.title: Recurrence for the guesses of permutation Wordle

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a strategy, that is, a permutation $S_m$ of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ for every $m$, and let $\pi$ be a permutation of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. The guesses $\gamma_1, \gamma_2, \dots$ of permutation Wordle with strategy $S$ and secret $\pi$ are the maps from $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to itself defined recursively: $\gamma_1$ is the identity, and $\gamma_{r+1}$ is the guess that one round of the game with strategy $S$…
nodes.title: Guesses of permutation Wordle

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a strategy, that is, a permutation $S_m$ of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ for every $m$, let $\pi$ be a permutation of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $g$ be a map from $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to itself. If $g(i) = \pi(i)$ at a position $i$, then the guess that one round of permutation Wordle with strategy $S$ and secret $\pi$ produces from $g$ also takes the value $g(i)$ at $i$.
nodes.title: Correct positions stay locked

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a strategy, that is, a permutation $S_m$ of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ for every $m$, let $\pi$ be a permutation of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (the secret), and let $g$ be a map from $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to itself (the current guess). Let $I$ be the set of incorrect positions, the $k$ with $g(k) \ne \pi(k)$, and let $m$ be the number of elements of $I$. The next guess agrees with $g$ at every position outside $I$ and…
nodes.title: One round of permutation Wordle

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a strategy, that is, a permutation $S_m$ of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ for every $m$, and let $\pi$ be a permutation of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then permutation Wordle with strategy $S$ and secret $\pi$ ends after exactly one guess if and only if $\pi$ is the identity.
nodes.title: Games won with the first guess

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a strategy, that is, a permutation $S_m$ of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ for every $m$, let $\pi$ be a permutation of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $\gamma_1, \gamma_2, \dots$ be the guesses of permutation Wordle with strategy $S$ and secret $\pi$. For a natural number $r$, the game ends after exactly $r$ guesses when $r \ge 1$, $\gamma_r = \pi$, and $\gamma_j \ne \pi$ for every $j$ with $1 \le j < r$.
nodes.title: Permutation Wordle games solved in a given number of guesses

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $g$ be a map from $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to itself. Applying $\sigma$ to the entries of $g$ along the set of all positions $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, listed in increasing order, gives the map $g \circ \sigma^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Permuting along all positions

nodes.summary: Let $I$ be a subset of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $k$ elements, listed in increasing order as $i_0 < i_1 < \dots < i_{k-1}$, let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$, and let $g$ be a map from $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to itself. Applying $\sigma$ to $g$ along $I$ gives the map that takes the value $g(i_j)$ at $i_{\sigma(j)}$ for every $j < k$ and agrees with $g$ outside $I$.
nodes.title: Permuting the entries of a map along a set of positions
Number Theory

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
